To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the effects of higher-education institutions on student satisfactions and perceptions are long-term, (b) the effects of the institution are greater for students who attended college more recently, (c) the effects of institutions on student satisfations and perceptions vary by student characteristics and the nature of the educational experience, (d) student perceptions of their experiences at the college or university are important predictors of their later satisfactions with higher education, and (e) student satisfactions with higher educa tion
(1) the effects of college on students' educational satisfactions and perceptions of their educational experiences are positive, but (2) these effects are not large, and (3) they are not uniform.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of college on students' satisfactions with college and with their perceptions of the educational process and its outcomes.
the long-term effects of college on students' satisfactions and perceptions.
the effects of college characteristics and student experiences on educational satisfactions and perceptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the college experience, in the aggregate, is one of the most important experiences in a young man's life, that the effects of the college experience are not limited to the years of college but extend over a long period of years, and that the most significant effects of the college environment are not limited to a few areas of the student's life but extend into almost every aspect of his life [33, p. 5].
the college experience has a positive effect on student attitudes and behaviors, and that these effects are not simply a reflection of pre-existing differences among students.
higher education, as a whole, has been a force for social mobility and for the development of the individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more the student is exposed to the college environment, the more he will be socialized.

students who are more involved in college activities and who have more positive experiences with faculty and other students are likely to be more satisfied with the education they receive and with their college experiences.
the college experience has been shown to affect the life course of students in ways that are both beneficial and deleterious.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be surprised to learn that students' experiences in college can affect the way they feel about their college and the way they feel in general.
the effects of college are not just a function of what happens in the classroom but of the whole student experience.
the college experience matters, and it matters in a variety of different ways.
